proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(f=f_{C0}\) and \(g=f_{C1}\) for the inner problem.  We first prove the scalar--harmonic linearization for a generic selected no-cut transport
\[
 F(x)=x+a+\nabla\phi(x),\qquad F\#(f\,dx)=g\,dx,qquad \int_{\mathbb T^2}\phi=0.
\tag{1}
\]
By ass:density-positivity and the applicable one of ass:inner-ellipticity and ass:outer-ellipticity,
\[
 c\leq f\leq C,qquad \lambda I_2\preceq DF\preceq\Lambda I_2.
\tag{2}
\]
Consequently the symmetric coefficient \(A_F=f(DF)^{-1}\) satisfies
\[
 \frac c\Lambda I_2\preceq A_F\preceq\frac C\lambda I_2.
\tag{3}
\]
On the space of mean-zero periodic functions, the energy
\(u\mapsto\frac12\int\nabla u^{\mathsf T}A_F\nabla u-\langle r,u\rangle\)
is strictly convex and coercive by (3) and the periodic Poincar\'e inequality.  Minimization over finite Fourier sums followed by completion therefore constructs the unique weak solution of
\(-\operatorname{div}(A_F\nabla u)=r\), for every mean-zero \(r\in H^{-1}\), and testing the Galerkin equations before passage to the limit gives
\[
 \lVert\nabla u\rVert_2\leq C\lVert r\rVert_{H^{-1}}.
\tag{4}
\]

The finite-dimensional equation comes from transport optimality.  Ass:lift-regularity places the graph in one smooth squared-distance chart.  In that chart use the Lagrangian
\[
 \mathcal K(F,\eta)=\frac12\int|F(x)-x|^2f(x)\,dx
 +\int\eta(F(x))f(x)\,dx-\int\eta(y)g(y)\,dy.
\tag{5}
\]
Stationarity in \(F\) and differentiation in \(x\) give, respectively,
\[
 \nabla\eta(F(x))=x-F(x),
 \qquad I_2+D^2\eta(F(x))=(DF(x))^{-1}.
\tag{6}
\]
For a harmonic velocity \(b\in\mathbb R^2\), write its feasible velocity as
\[
 v_b=b+\nabla\psi_b,qquad \int\psi_b=0.
\tag{7}
\]
Differentiating \(g(F)\det DF=f\), with \(f,g\) fixed, and using the Piola identity yields
\[
 \operatorname{div}(A_Fv_b)=0,
 \qquad -\operatorname{div}(A_F\nabla\psi_b)=\operatorname{div}(A_Fb).
\tag{8}
\]
Thus (4) uniquely determines \(\psi_b\).  Let \(J_F(a;f,g)\) be the transport cost after the scalar mass equation has been solved at fixed \(a\).  At the stationary value of \(a\), equations (6)--(8) give the reduced Hessian identity
\[
 b^{\mathsf T}D_a^2J_F(a;f,g)b
 =\int v_b^{\mathsf T}A_Fv_b
 =\inf_{\substack{\psi\ {
m periodic}\\ \int\psi=0}}
   \int(b+\nabla\psi)^{\mathsf T}A_F(b+\nabla\psi).
\tag{9}
\]
Indeed, (8) is the Euler equation of the displayed energy, while the first equality follows by differentiating (5) twice and substituting (6); all acceleration terms vanish by the first-order equations.  Since \(\int\nabla\psi_b=0\), (3) and (9) imply
\[
 b^{\mathsf T}D_a^2J_F(a;f,g)b
 \geq\frac c\Lambda\int|b+\nabla\psi_b|^2
 =\frac c\Lambda\bigl(|b|^2+\lVert\nabla\psi_b\rVert_2^2\bigr)
 \geq\frac c\Lambda|b|^2.
\tag{10}
\]
This is uniform harmonic coercivity and uses no additional nondegeneracy assumption.

Let \((f_t,g_t)\) be a smooth density path and write \((\dot f,\dot g)\) for its tangent.  Decompose
\(\dot F=b_F+\nabla u_F\), with \(\int u_F=0\).  Differentiation of the mass equation gives
\[
 \dot f=\det(DF)\dot g\circ F+
 \operatorname{div}\{A_F(b_F+\nabla u_F)\}.
\tag{11}
\]
Hence, for \(r_F=\det(DF)\dot g\circ F-\dot f\),
\[
 -\operatorname{div}(A_F\nabla u_F)
 =r_F+\operatorname{div}(A_Fb_F).
\tag{12}
\]
The right side integrates to zero.  Define the density-forcing vector by
\[
 d^{\mathsf T}\mathfrak s_F[\dot f,\dot g]
 :=\left.\frac d{dt}\right|_{t=0}D_aJ_F(a;f_t,g_t)[d],
 \qquad d\in\mathbb R^2.
\tag{13}
\]
Differentiating the two reduced stationarity equations gives
\[
 D_a^2J_F(a;f,g)b_F=-\mathfrak s_F[\dot f,\dot g],
 \qquad
 b_F=-\{D_a^2J_F(a;f,g)\}^{-1}\mathfrak s_F[\dot f,\dot g].
\tag{14}
\]
Equations (4), (10), (12), and (14) prove uniform invertibility of the augmented scalar--harmonic system.

We also need the asserted Riesz bound.  Differentiate (5) once in the density path and once in the harmonic direction \(d\).  By (6) and (11), all derivatives of the constrained map cancel.  The remaining terms are integrals of \(\dot f\) or \(\dot g\) against uniformly smooth functions and the energy pairing
\[
 \int v_d^{\mathsf T}A_F\nabla u_0,
 \qquad -\operatorname{div}(A_F\nabla u_0)=r_F.
\tag{15}
\]
Changing variables by \(F\), then applying (4), (9), and Cauchy--Schwarz, proves
\[
 |\mathfrak s_F[\dot f,\dot g]|
 \leq C\left(
 \left\lVert\frac{\dot f}{f}\right\rVert_{L^2(f)}+
 \left\lVert\frac{\dot g}{g}\right\rVert_{L^2(g)}
 \right).
\tag{16}
\]
Solving the scalar adjoint in (12) and the two finite-dimensional adjoints in (14), and integrating (13) by parts, therefore gives functions \(\zeta_{F,f}\) and \(\zeta_{F,g}\) such that every coordinate of \(b_F\) equals
\[
 \int\zeta_{F,f}\dot f+\int\zeta_{F,g}\dot g,
 \qquad
 \lVert\zeta_{F,f}\rVert_{L^2(f)}+
 \lVert\zeta_{F,g}\rVert_{L^2(g)}\leq C.
\tag{17}
\]
Uniformity follows from (2)--(3), the uniform density smoothness bound, and the common branch margin.

Apply the system first to \(p\).  With \(A=f_{C0}S^{-1}\), \(b_p=\dot a_p\), and scalar derivative \(u_p\),
\[
 \mathcal L_Au_p=\det(S)\delta_{C1}\circ p-\delta_{C0}
 +\operatorname{div}(Ab_p).
\tag{18}
\]
In treated-post coordinates take the mean-zero representative of
\[
 \bar u_p(y)=b_p^{\mathsf T}\{R_0(y)-y\}+u_p(R_0(y)).
\tag{19}
\]
Equivariance makes this expression periodic up to an additive constant, and the chain rule gives
\[
 b_p+\nabla\bar u_p(y)=D(y)^{\mathsf T}
 \{b_p+\nabla u_p(R_0(y))\}.
\tag{20}
\]
The Piola change of variables in (18) now yields
\[
 \mathcal L_{\mathsf C}\bar u_p
 =e_{C1}-e_{C0}+\operatorname{div}(\mathsf Cb_p).
\tag{21}
\]

The generated law must also be differentiated.  For every smooth periodic \(\zeta\),
\[
 \left.\frac d{dt}\right|_0\int\zeta\,dq_t
 =\int\zeta(p(x))\delta_{T0}(x)\,dx
 +\int\nabla\zeta(p(x))^{\mathsf T}
     \{b_p+\nabla u_p(x)\}f_{T0}(x)\,dx.
\tag{22}
\]
Changing variables and integrating by parts gives
\[
 \dot q=p\#\delta_{T0}
 -\operatorname{div}_z\!left[q(z)
 \{b_p+\nabla u_p\}(p^{-1}(z))\right].
\tag{23}
\]
Pulling (23) through \(T\) and using (20) gives
\[
 \det(H)\dot q\circ T=e_{T0}-
 \operatorname{div}\!left[BD^{-\mathsf T}
 \{b_p+\nabla\bar u_p\}\right].
\tag{24}
\]
The population mass equation for \(R_0\) is
\[
 f_{T1}(y)=f_{T0}(R_0(y))\det D(y).
\tag{25}
\]
Using \(D=S(R_0)^{-1}H\) and symmetry of \(S,H\), direct multiplication gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \alpha\mathsf C
 &=\frac{f_{T0}(R_0)}{f_{C0}(R_0)}\det(D)D^{-1}
   \{f_{C0}(R_0)S(R_0)^{-1}\}D^{-\mathsf T}\\
 &=f_{T1}H^{-1}S(R_0)H^{-1}=BD^{-\mathsf T}.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{26}
\]
No commutation of \(S\) and \(H\) is used.  Combining (21), (24), (26), and the product rule yields
\[
 \det(H)\dot q\circ T=e_{T0}+\alpha(e_{C1}-e_{C0})
 -(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\cdot\{b_p+\nabla\bar u_p\}.
\tag{27}
\]
Apply the augmented system to \(T\).  With \(b_T=\dot a_T\) and scalar derivative \(u_T\),
\[
 \mathcal L_Bu_T=e_{T0}-e_{T1}+\alpha(e_{C1}-e_{C0})
 -(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\cdot\{b_p+\nabla\bar u_p\}
 +\operatorname{div}(Bb_T).
\tag{28}
\]
By (21),
\[
 \nabla\bar u_p=
 \nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0(e_{C1}-e_{C0})
 +\nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0
   \operatorname{div}(\mathsf Cb_p).
\tag{29}
\]
Substitution of (29) in (28), followed by addition of \(b_T\), is exactly \(\mathcal D_P[\delta]\) and \(\mathcal H_P[\delta]\) in def:nested-derivative.

It remains to justify Fr\'echet, rather than only pathwise, differentiability.  Fix \(\vartheta=1/4\), let \(u=(u_g)_{g\in\mathcal G}\) be a zero-integral perturbation, and set
\[
 U_1=\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{1,\vartheta}},
 \qquad U_0=\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{0,\vartheta}}.
\tag{30}
\]
When the \(C^{2,\vartheta}\) norm is within the common branch chart, the exact identities
\[
 \det(M+E)-\det M-\operatorname{cof}(M):E=\det E,
\qquad
 \frac1{a+v}-\frac1a+\frac v{a^2}=
 \frac{v^2}{a^2(a+v)}
\tag{31}
\]
show that determinant and reciprocal residuals are bounded in \(C^{0,\vartheta}\) by \(CU_1U_0\).  The integral Taylor identity
\[
 q(x+v)-q(x)-Dq(x)v
 =\int_0^1\{Dq(x+tv)-Dq(x)\}v\,dt
\tag{32}
\]
and its inverse-map analogue give the same bound for composition and inverse residuals.  Differentiating (5) on this chart gives the bound \(CU_1U_0\) for the harmonic-stationarity residual as well.  The scalar inverse bound (4) and harmonic Schur-complement bound (10) therefore imply, for a single map,
\[
 |a_{F,u}-a_F-b_F|+
 \lVert\phi_{F,u}-\phi_F-u_F\rVert_{C^{2,\vartheta}}
 \leq CU_1U_0.
\tag{33}
\]
Apply (33) first to \(p\), expand the exact generated density
\(f_{C1}(f_{T0}/f_{C0})\circ p^{-1}\) using (31)--(32), and apply (33) to \(T\).  This proves
\[
 \max_{1\leq j\leq J}\left\lVert
 \widetilde T_{P+u}(\widetilde y_j)-\widetilde T_P(\widetilde y_j)
 -\mathcal D_P[u]_j\right\rVert\leq CU_1U_0.
\tag{34}
\]

Finally, (16)--(17), applied successively to the inner and outer systems and to (23), show that every coordinate of \(b_p,b_T\), and every smooth elliptic corrector multiplying them in \(\mathcal H_P\), has a cellwise \(L^2(P_g)\) Riesz score bounded by one common constant.  For a centered kernel tangent its score is \(K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\zeta-P_g(K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\zeta)\), whose \(L^2(P_g)\) norm is bounded by Young's inequality and ass:density-positivity.  By lem:elliptic-green-gradient-bound, with the torus localization proved in the proof of lem:uniform-critical-estimates below, the leading Green score has squared \(L^2\) norm at most
\[
 C\int_h^1r^{-2}r\,dr+C\leq C\log(1/h).
\tag{35}
\]
Thus the normalized harmonic variance is \(O(1/\log(1/h))\), and Cauchy--Schwarz makes every normalized Green--harmonic covariance \(O(1/\sqrt{\log(1/h)})\).  All bounds are uniform over \(\mathcal F_s\).  This proves every assertion.

Let \(\vartheta=1/4\), and, for \(k=0,1,2\), put
\[
 q_{k,n}=\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{,2+2k+2\vartheta}}}
          +h_n^{,s-k-\vartheta}.
\tag{1}
\]
These are exactly the three displayed rates in the statement.  We first establish the pilot bounds.  Differentiating the periodized kernel \(k\) times, applying the exponential-moment inequality
\(e^x\leq1+x+x^2e^{|x|}/2\) to each bounded centered summand, and taking a union bound on a torus lattice of mesh \(h_n n^{-3}\), gives
\[
 \mathbb P_P\!\left(
 \lVert\widetilde f_g-E_P\widetilde f_g\rVert_{C^{k,\vartheta}}>z
 \right)
 \leq Cn^C\exp\{-c n h_n^{2+2k+2\vartheta}z^2\}
\tag{2}
\]
for \(0<z\leq1\), uniformly in \(P\) and \(g\).  To pass from the lattice to the torus, apply the mean-value theorem to the differentiated kernel on every lattice square; the deterministic oscillation is absorbed by the same bound with derivative order \(k+1\).  Integration of (2) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P\lVert\widetilde f_g-E_P\widetilde f_g\rVert_{C^{k,\vartheta}}^4
 \leq C\left\{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{2+2k+2\vartheta}}\right\}^{2}.
\tag{3}
\]
Taylor expansion of \(f_g(x-hu)\) through order \(s-1\), followed by ass:kernel-order and ass:kernel-mass, gives
\[
 \lVert E_P\widetilde f_g-f_g\rVert_{C^{k,\vartheta}}
 \leq Ch_n^{s-k-\vartheta}.
\tag{4}
\]
Equations (3)--(4) prove the asserted fourth-moment bound when \(k=1\).  With \(k=2\), a fixed threshold in (2), and absorption of the polynomial prefactor, they also give
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb P_P\!\left(
 \max_g\lVert\widetilde f_g-f_g\rVert_{C^{2,\vartheta}}>\epsilon_0
 \right)\leq C_0e^{-c_0nh_n^{13/2}}.
\tag{5}
\]
By lem:mixed-bandwidth-feasibility and ass:polynomial-bandwidth,
\[
 q_{2,n}=o(1),\qquad q_{0,n}/h_n=o(1),qquad
 \sqrt{n/L_n}\,q_{1,n}q_{0,n}=o(1).
\tag{6}
\]

We next prove the critical Green estimate, including the torus localization.  Fix a pole \(y\) and write \(B_y=B(y)\).  In a coordinate ball of radius less than \(\delta_0/8\), let
\[
 \Gamma_y(z)=-\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{\det B_y}}
 \log|B_y^{-1/2}(z-y)|.
\tag{7}
\]
Choose a smooth cutoff \(\chi\) supported in the ball and equal to one near \(y\).  Before testing any singular expression, define
\[
 F_y(z)=\{B(z)-B_y\}\chi(z)\nabla\Gamma_y(z)
\tag{8}
\]
and construct \(w_y\in H^1_0\) as the minimizer of the coercive energy with weak forcing \(\operatorname{div}F_y\) plus the bounded cutoff terms.  This construction is legitimate because uniform \(C^{0,\vartheta}\) control of \(B\) gives
\[
 |F_y(z)|\leq C|z-y|^{-1+\vartheta},
 \qquad F_y\in L^2.
\tag{9}
\]
Only after this construction do we test the weak equation and obtain \(\lVert\nabla w_y\rVert_2\leq C\).  The difference between the periodic Green function and the resulting local Dirichlet Green function is \(B\)-harmonic in a smaller ball.  Its gradient is uniformly bounded there by the interior estimate in lem:elliptic-green-gradient-bound, while compactness and the normalized energy estimate bound it away from the pole.  Rescaling (8) on dyadic annuli and applying the same interior estimate yields the more precise expansion
\[
 \nabla_zG_B(y,z)=\nabla\Gamma_y(z)+R_y(z),
 \qquad |R_y(z)|\leq C|z-y|^{-1+\vartheta},
 \qquad \sup_y\lVert R_y\rVert_2\leq C.
\tag{10}
\]
This proves the required periodic statement rather than importing a boundary-domain estimate across the torus seam.

Apply Fubini before estimating a KDE response.  Every leading cell-
\(g\) influence at point \(y_j\) can then be written
\[
 \psi^0_{g,j,h}(x)=K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\zeta^0_{g,j}(x)
 -P_g(K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\zeta^0_{g,j}),
\tag{11}
\]
where \(\zeta^0_{g,j}\) is the frozen expression (7), pulled back to the original cell coordinate by either \(R_0\) or \(T\), and multiplied by the corresponding coefficient \(1\) or \(\alpha(y_j)\).  The exact change of variables cancels the Jacobian in the transformed kernel tangent.  Thus no approximation of a nonlinear kernel argument has been made in (11).  Taylor's formula for the smooth pullback \(\Phi\), uniformly for \(|v|\leq Ch\), is
\[
 \Phi(x+v)-\Phi(x)-D\Phi(x)v
 =\int_0^1(1-t)D^2\Phi(x+tv)[v,v],dt,
 \qquad |\cdot|\leq Ch^2.
\tag{12}
\]
Together with (10), (12) shows that the difference between the exact first-order-coordinate Green influence and \(\zeta^0_{g,j}\) has uniformly bounded \(L^2(P_g)\) norm.  The second, order-minus-two term in def:nested-derivative has kernel bounded by
\[
 C\int_{\mathbb T^2}\frac{dz}{d(z,y_j)d(z,x)}
 \leq C\{1+|\log d(x,y_j)|\},
\tag{13}
\]
and hence also belongs uniformly to \(L^2\).  The weighted-Hodge construction in thm:nested-derivative gives the same bound for every harmonic term.  Young's inequality applied only after these \(L^2\) bounds have been established proves
\[
 \lVert\Psi_{g,h}-\psi^0_{g,h}\rVert_{L^2(P_g)}\leq C,
 \qquad \lVert\Psi_{g,h}\rVert_{L^2(P_g)}\leq C\sqrt{\log(1/h)}.
\tag{14}
\]

For clarity, the mollification calculation behind (14) is explicit.  A frozen singular field \(z^0(x)\) satisfies \(|z^0(x)|\leq C/d(x,x_0)\).  On \(d(x,x_0)>Ch\), kernel symmetry and (12) imply
\[
 |K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*z^0(x)-z^0(x)|\leq Ch,d(x,x_0)^{-2},
\tag{15}
\]
whereas on \(d(x,x_0)\leq Ch\) both sides are bounded by \(C/h\).  Radial integration gives
\[
 \int_{d\leq Ch}|K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*z^0|^2=O(1),
 \qquad
 \int_{d>Ch}|K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*z^0-z^0|^2=O(1).
\tag{16}
\]
The same split, with fourth powers, gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_g}\lVert\Psi_{g,h}(X)\rVert^4\leq Ch^{-2}.
\tag{17}
\]
The centering terms are bounded because \(1/d(\cdot,x_0)\) is integrable in dimension two.  Equations (10)--(17) prove the first two score assertions in the lemma, including all generated-target and harmonic pieces.

We now treat estimated coefficients and moving poles.  On the event in (5), the two augmented systems of thm:nested-derivative and their adjoints have common ellipticity and Schur-complement constants.  Their deterministic stability estimates and (1)--(4) imply
\[
 \epsilon_n^{\rm coef}:=max_{g,r}
 \{\lVert\widehat B^{(-r)}-B\rVert_{C^1}
   +\lVert\widehat{\mathsf C}^{(-r)}-\mathsf C\rVert_{C^1}
   +\lVert\widehat\alpha^{(-r)}-\alpha\rVert_{C^1}\}=o_{\mathbb P}(1),
\tag{18}
\]
and every estimated pole obeys
\[
 d_n^{\rm pole}\leq Cq_{0,n}=o_{\mathbb P}(h_n).
\tag{19}
\]
For a mollified \(1/d\) field, differentiation with respect to its pole and (16) give
\[
 \lVert K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*z^0(\cdot-d)-K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*z^0\rVert_2
 \leq C|d|/h.
\tag{20}
\]
The resolvent identity for each scalar or adjoint inverse,
\[
 \mathcal L_{\widehat B}^{-1}-\mathcal L_B^{-1}
 =\mathcal L_{\widehat B}^{-1}
   (\mathcal L_B-\mathcal L_{\widehat B})\mathcal L_B^{-1},
\tag{21}
\]
and the analogous finite-dimensional Schur-complement identity show that coefficient perturbations contribute at most
\(C\epsilon_n^{\rm coef}\sqrt{L_n}\) in \(L^2\).  The order-minus-two and harmonic parts contribute \(o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{L_n})\) by their bounded \(L^2\) envelopes.  From (18)--(21),
\[
 \max_{g,r}L_n^{-1/2}
 \lVert\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}-\Psi_{g,h_n}\rVert_{L^2(P_g)}
 =o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\tag{22}
\]
The pointwise version of the same annular split is bounded by \(C/(d+h_n)\); raising it to the fourth power and integrating proves, on the good event,
\[
 \max_{g,r}\mathbb E_{P_g}
 \lVert\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}(X)\rVert^4\leq Ch_n^{-2}.
\tag{23}
\]

It remains to prove the nonlinear assertion.  Equations (31)--(33) in the proof of thm:nested-derivative apply uniformly on the event
\(\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{2,\vartheta}}<\epsilon_0\).  They give the stronger two-endpoint estimate
\[
 \max_j\left\lVert
 \widetilde T_{P+u}(\widetilde y_j)-\widetilde T_P(\widetilde y_j)
 -\mathcal D_P[u]_j\right\rVert
 \leq C\left(\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{1,\vartheta}}\right)
          \left(\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{0,\vartheta}}\right).
\tag{24}
\]
Since the \(C^{0,\vartheta}\) norm is bounded by the \(C^{1,\vartheta}\) norm, (24) implies the displayed quadratic inequality in the lemma.  Combining (3)--(6) and (24) proves that its stochastic value is
\(o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{L_n/n})\).  The kernel moment expansion gives the deterministic transport bias \(O(h_n^{s-2})\), and lem:mixed-bandwidth-feasibility makes its normalized value vanish.

Finally, on the event in (5), \(\lVert\widetilde f_g-f_g\rVert_\infty<c/2\), so clipping is inactive.  Ass:kernel-mass and periodization give \(\int\widetilde f_g=1\), hence the normalizer is exactly one.  Stability of the augmented systems plus ass:lift-regularity keeps both maps on their population branches, preserves ellipticity, and, by (19), places every pilot pole within \(o_{\mathbb P}(h_n)\) of its population pole.  This proves all assertions of the lemma.

By lem:uniform-critical-estimates, for every cell and grid point the exact score is its mollified frozen \(1/r\) Green field plus an \(L^2(P_g)\)-bounded remainder.  Therefore the remainder variance divided by \(L_n\) is \(O(L_n^{-1})\), and its cross-covariance with the leading score divided by \(L_n\) is \(O(L_n^{-1/2})\), uniformly by Cauchy--Schwarz.  This applies in particular to the complete harmonic term from thm:nested-derivative and to the order-minus-two generated-target term.

Fix \(y_j\), put \(B_j=B(y_j)\), and use the frozen fundamental solution
\[
 \Gamma_j(z)=-\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{\det B_j}}
 \log|B_j^{-1/2}z|.
\tag{1}
\]
With \(z=B_j^{1/2}r\omega\), \(\omega\in\mathbb S^1\), and
\(\int_{\mathbb S^1}\omega\omega^{\mathsf T}d\omega=\pi I_2\), direct integration gives
\[
 \int_{h<|z|<r_0}\nabla\Gamma_j(z)\nabla\Gamma_j(z)^{\mathsf T}dz
 =\frac{B_j^{-1}}{4\pi\sqrt{\det B_j}}\log(1/h)+O(1).
\tag{2}
\]
The inner and outer boundaries may be replaced by uniformly nondegenerate ellipses because this changes only the \(O(1)\) term.  Lem:uniform-critical-estimates proves that convolution by \(K_h^{\mathrm{per}}\), the variable coefficient, and the nonlinear coordinate pullback also alter (2) by \(o(\log(1/h))\), uniformly.

We compute the four local intensities without discarding within-cell cross terms.  The mass identities are
\[
 f_{C1}(T(y))\det H(y)=f_{C0}(R_0(y))\det D(y),
 \qquad f_{T0}(R_0(y))\det D(y)=f_{T1}(y).
\tag{3}
\]
For either control cell, the squared leading multiplier is \(\alpha(y_j)^2\), while the pullback intensity before that multiplication is
\(f_{C0}(R_0(y_j))\det D(y_j)=f_{T1}(y_j)/\alpha(y_j)\).  Hence each control cell has local intensity \(\alpha(y_j)f_{T1}(y_j)\).  Each treated cell has local intensity \(f_{T1}(y_j)\).  The two appearances of a control noise in def:nested-derivative were combined before squaring; their order-minus-two and harmonic parts are in the bounded remainder, so their cross-products with the leading part are exactly among the vanishing terms above.  Independence in ass:four-sample-design removes cross-cell, but not within-cell, covariances.  It follows from (2)--(3) and ass:cell-ratios that the \((j,j)\) block tends to
\[
 f_{T1}(y_j)w_j\frac{B_j^{-1}}{4\pi\sqrt{\det B_j}},
 \quad
 w_j=\alpha(y_j)(\rho_{C0}^{-1}+\rho_{C1}^{-1})
      +\rho_{T0}^{-1}+\rho_{T1}^{-1}.
\tag{4}
\]
Since \(B_j=f_{T1}(y_j)H(y_j)^{-1}\),
\[
 f_{T1}(y_j)w_j\frac{B_j^{-1}}{4\pi\sqrt{\det B_j}}
 =\frac{w_j\sqrt{\det H(y_j)}H(y_j)}{4\pi f_{T1}(y_j)}=V_j.
\tag{5}
\]
If \(j\neq k\), ass:fixed-separated-grid and invertibility of the pullbacks keep the two poles a fixed positive distance apart.  Near either pole the other singular field is bounded, so their product is locally integrable; the cross-block covariance is therefore \(O(1)/L_n=o(1)\).  Equations (4)--(5), summed over the four independent cells, prove
\(\sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\lVert\Sigma_{h_n}(P)-V(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\to0\).

Moreover, ass:density-positivity, ass:outer-ellipticity, and
\(1\leq\rho_g\leq\bar\rho\) give
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(V_j)
 \geq\frac{\lambda^2}{4\pi C\bar\rho}>0,
\tag{6}
\]
so the asserted positive definiteness is uniform.

On the good event of lem:uniform-critical-estimates, clipping is inactive, the normalizers equal one, and both estimated lifts use their population branches.  Apply the translation-aware expansion in that lemma with
\(u_g=\widetilde f_g-f_g\).  Since \(\widehat\tau\) is the negative of the lifted-map displacement increment, Fubini and centering give
\[
 \widehat\tau-\tau(P)
 =-\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}\frac1{n_g}\sum_{i=1}^{n_g}
   \Psi_{g,h_n}(X_{g,i})+b_n+r_n,
\tag{1}
\]
where
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\lVert b_n\rVert\leq Ch_n^{s-2},
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb P_P
 \{\sqrt{n/L_n}\lVert r_n\rVert>\epsilon\}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{2}
\]
The first bound follows by applying the order-minus-two derivative to the order-
\(s\) kernel bias.  For the second, equation (24) in lem:uniform-critical-estimates and its pilot moment bounds give
\[
 \sqrt{n/L_n}\,\mathbb E_P^{1/2}\lVert r_n\rVert^2
 \leq C\sqrt{n/L_n}\left{
 \frac{\log n}{nh_n^{9/2}}+h_n^{2s-5/2}\right}=o(1),
\tag{3}
\]
by ass:polynomial-bandwidth.  Also
\(\sqrt{n/L_n}h_n^{s-2}\to0\) by lem:mixed-bandwidth-feasibility.

Set
\[
 W_{g,i,n}=-\sqrt{n/L_n}\,n_g^{-1}\Psi_{g,h_n}(X_{g,i}).
\tag{4}
\]
The variables in (4) are independent and centered by ass:four-sample-design.  The fourth-moment estimate in lem:uniform-critical-estimates and bounded cell ratios give
\[
 \sum_{g,i}\mathbb E_P\lVert W_{g,i,n}\rVert^4
 \leq\frac{C}{nh_n^2L_n^2}=o(1).
\tag{5}
\]
The last limit follows from the bandwidth consequences in lem:mixed-bandwidth-feasibility.  For any fixed \(t\in\mathbb R^{2J}\), expand
\(E e^{it^{\mathsf T}W}=1-\tfrac12E(t^{\mathsf T}W)^2+R\), where
\(|R|\leq C_tE|W|^3\) on \(|W|\leq1\) and the complement is bounded using its fourth moment.  Summing, (5) makes the total remainder vanish uniformly.  Taking products over \((g,i)\) therefore proves that the characteristic function of \(\sum_{g,i}W_{g,i,n}\) differs uniformly from that of the centered Gaussian with covariance \(\Sigma_{h_n}(P)+o(1)\) by \(o(1)\).  Tightness follows from the uniform second-moment bound.  Lem:full-critical-covariance then gives, uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal F_s\),
\[
 \sum_{g,i}W_{g,i,n}\Rightarrow N(0,V(P))
\tag{6}
\]
in bounded-Lipschitz distance.  Equations (1)--(3) transfer (6) to the stated statistic.

The exceptional event in lem:uniform-critical-estimates has probability bounded by
\(C_0e^{-c_0nh_n^{13/2}}=o(1)\).  On it, def:translation-aware-lift uses a measurable fallback; both the regular intrinsic displacement and the fallback displacement are bounded on the compact torus.  Hence alteration on that event is negligible in bounded-Lipschitz distance.  This also proves the asserted uniform branch-selection and fallback claims.

Fix \(P_0\in\operatorname{int}(\mathcal F_s)\) and put
\(\Theta(P)=\upsilon^{\mathsf T}\tau_1(P)\).  All constants in this proof may depend on the fixed center and its strict margins.  By thm:nested-derivative, the cell-
\(g_\star\) derivative of \(\Theta\) is the leading outer Green functional with representer \(\varphi_{g_\star}\), plus order-minus-two and weighted-Hodge harmonic functionals having bounded \(L^2(P_{0g_\star})\) representers.

Let \(x_\star\) be the unique pullback of \(y_1\) to the \(g_\star\)-cell coordinates.  The parametrix construction in lem:uniform-critical-estimates and invertibility of all coordinate pullbacks give, on a fixed ball about \(x_\star\),
\[
 \varphi_{g_\star}(x)=
 \frac{b_{g_\star}^{\mathsf T}(x-x_\star)}
 {|E_{g_\star}(x-x_\star)|^2}+r_{g_\star}(x),
 \qquad b_{g_\star}\neq0,
\tag{1}
\]
where \(E_{g_\star}\) is invertible and, for \(0\leq m\leq s\),
\[
 |\nabla^m r_{g_\star}(x)|
 \leq C|x-x_\star|^{-m}\{1+|\log|x-x_\star||\}.
\tag{2}
\]
The numerator in (1) is nonzero because \(\upsilon\neq0\), the pullbacks have full rank, the outer Green matrix is positive definite, and the cell multiplier is either \(1\) or the positive number \(\alpha(y_1)\).

An anisotropic polar change of variables in (1), followed by (2), gives a number \(a_{g_\star}(P_0)>0\) such that
\[
 \int\chi_\varepsilon^2\varphi_{g_\star}^2\,dP_{0g_\star}
 =a_{g_\star}(P_0)\log(1/\varepsilon)+O_{P_0}(1).
\tag{3}
\]
The centering integral is bounded because \(1/|x-x_\star|\) is locally integrable in two dimensions.  Hence centering changes (3) by only \(O_{P_0}(1)\), proving the asserted two-sided logarithmic bounds.  Leibniz's rule, (1)--(2), and the transition bounds defining \(\chi_\varepsilon\) also give, separately for every \(0\leq m\leq s\),
\[
 \lVert\nabla^m(\chi_\varepsilon\varphi_{g_\star})\rVert_\infty
 \leq C_{P_0}\varepsilon^{-m-1}.
\tag{4}
\]
After centering and multiplication by \(f_{0g_\star}\), the case \(m=s\) proves the claimed \(C^s\) envelope.

Set
\[
 u_n=\frac{\zeta\ell_{\varepsilon_n,g_\star}}
 {\sqrt n\,\lVert\ell_{\varepsilon_n,g_\star}\rVert_{L^2(P_{0g_\star})}}.
\tag{5}
\]
It is centered under \(P_{0g_\star}\), so both alternatives have mass one.  Equations (3)--(5) imply
\[
 \lVert u_n\rVert_2=\zeta n^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 \lVert f_{0g_\star}u_n\rVert_{C^s}
 \leq\frac{C_{P_0}\zeta\varepsilon_n^{-s-1}}
 {\sqrt{n\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}}=o(1),
\tag{6}
\]
because \(\eta(s+1)<1/2\).  The case \(m=0\) in (4) gives \(\lVert u_n\rVert_\infty=o(1)\); therefore both densities are positive for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The strict interior margins of \(P_0\), continuity of the two augmented transport systems, and (6) retain density bounds, ellipticity, and the lift and cut-locus margins.

Membership in the causal class is also explicit.  For either sign let \(p\) and \(T\) be the transports generated by the perturbed four laws and set
\[
 h_0=\operatorname{id},\qquad \nu_C=P_{C0},\qquad
 \nu_T=P_{T0},\qquad h_1=p,qquad h_{1\star}=T^{-1}\circ p.
\tag{7}
\]
Then \(h_1\#\nu_C=P_{C1}\),
\(h_{1\star}\#\nu_T=T^{-1}\#(p\#P_{T0})=P_{T1}\), and
\(h_1\circ h_0^{-1}=p\), \(h_1\circ h_{1\star}^{-1}=T\).  The last two graphs are \(c_{\mathbb T}\)-cyclically monotone by their defining optimality.  Thus (7) verifies ass:cic-identification and proves membership in \(\mathcal F_s\).

For \(|v|\leq1/2\), \((\sqrt{1+v}-1)^2\leq v^2\).  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Hel}^2(P_{n,\pm,g_\star},P_{0g_\star})
 \leq\int u_n^2\,dP_{0g_\star}=\frac{\zeta^2}{n}.
\tag{8}
\]
All other cells are unchanged.  This proves neighborhood membership after choosing \(C_{P_0}\zeta^2\leq\kappa\).  Similarly,
\[
 \operatorname{Hel}^2(P_{n,+,g_\star},P_{n,-,g_\star})
 \leq C\zeta^2/n.
\tag{9}
\]
Since squared Hellinger distance of product laws is at most the sum of the component squared distances and \(n_{g_\star}=n\), (9) gives the claimed product bound; decreasing \(\zeta_0(P_0)\) makes it at most \(1/2\).

We prove separation with the corrected harmonic terms retained.  Centering \(\varphi_{g_\star}\) does not change its action on density tangents, and (1)--(3) give
\[
 \int\varphi_{g_\star}\ell_{\varepsilon,g_\star}\,dP_{0g_\star}
 =\lVert\ell_{\varepsilon,g_\star}\rVert_2^2+O_{P_0}(1).
\tag{10}
\]
Every order-minus-two or harmonic representer is bounded in \(L^2\), so its pairing with \(u_n\) is \(O_{P_0,\zeta}(n^{-1/2})\).  Hence
\[
 D\Theta_{P_0}[f_{0g_\star}u_n]
 =\frac{\zeta}{\sqrt n}\lVert\ell_{\varepsilon_n,g_\star}\rVert_2
 +O_{P_0,\zeta}(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{11}
\]
Use the mixed Fr\'echet remainder (34) from thm:nested-derivative separately for the positive and negative endpoints.  The order-specific bound (4), rather than its crude \(C^s\) consequence, gives
\[
 U_1\leq\frac{C\zeta\varepsilon_n^{-2}}
 {\sqrt{n\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}},
 \qquad
 U_0\leq\frac{C\zeta\varepsilon_n^{-1}}
 {\sqrt{n\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}}.
\tag{12}
\]
Thus each endpoint remainder is at most
\[
 CU_1U_0\leq
 \frac{C\zeta^2\varepsilon_n^{-3}}{n\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}
 =o\!\left(\zeta\sqrt{\frac{\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}n}\right),
\tag{13}
\]
because \(\eta<1/[2(s+1)]\leq1/18<1/6\).  Equations (3), (11), and (13) prove the displayed two-sided separation after decreasing \(c_1(P_0)\).

Finally, the bounded Riesz scores for \(b_p\) and \(b_T\) in thm:nested-derivative, positivity along both line segments, and (5) yield by integration
\[
 \lVert a_p(P_{n,\pm})-a_p(P_0)\rVert+
 \lVert a_T(P_{n,\pm})-a_T(P_0)\rVert
 \leq C_{P_0}\lVert u_n\rVert_2
 =O_{P_0,\zeta}(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{14}
\]
This is negligible relative to the logarithmic separation and completes the proof.

We first prove the upper bound.  On the good event from lem:uniform-critical-estimates, use expansion (1) in thm:joint-critical-clt.  Independence, the score second-moment bound, and the bounded cell ratios imply
\[
 \mathbb E_P\left\lVert
 \sum_g\frac1{n_g}\sum_i\Psi_{g,h_n}(X_{g,i})
 \right\rVert^2
 \leq C\frac{L_n}{n}.
\tag{1}
\]
The squared deterministic bias is at most \(Ch_n^{2(s-2)}\leq C/n\), because
\(a_h\geq1/[2(s-2)]\).  The mixed remainder and the fourth-moment pilot bound give
\[
 \mathbb E_P\lVert r_n\rVert^2
 \leq C\left\{\frac{\log n}{nh_n^{9/2}}+h_n^{2s-5/2}\right\}^2
 \leq C\frac{L_n}{n},
\tag{2}
\]
where the final inequality uses \(a_h<1/9\).  On the complementary event the translation-aware torus displacement and the measurable fallback are bounded, while (5) of lem:uniform-critical-estimates is exponentially small; its contribution is therefore \(o(L_n/n)\).  Equations (1)--(2) prove the class-uniform upper bound.

For the lower bound, fix the alternatives in lem:green-local-alternatives and let
\[
 \Delta_n=\left|\upsilon^{\mathsf T}
 \{\tau(P_{n,+})-\tau(P_{n,-})\}_1\right|.
\tag{3}
\]
That lemma and \(\log(1/\varepsilon_n)=\eta\log n=(\eta/a_h)L_n\) give
\[
 \Delta_n^2\geq c(P_0)\zeta^2\frac{L_n}{n}.
\tag{4}
\]
Choose \(\zeta>0\) small enough that the product squared Hellinger distance is at most \(1/2\), and then choose \(\kappa(P_0)\) so that both alternatives belong to
\(\mathcal N_n(P_0,\kappa(P_0))\).  If \(Q_{n,+}\) and \(Q_{n,-}\) denote their product sampling laws, Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \lVert Q_{n,+}-Q_{n,-}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \leq\operatorname{Hel}(Q_{n,+},Q_{n,-})\leq2^{-1/2}.
\tag{5}
\]
For any estimator \(\widetilde\tau_n\), decide between the two alternatives by whichever value in (3) is closer to
\(\upsilon^{\mathsf T}\widetilde\tau_{n,1}\).  On a wrong decision the squared scalar error is at least \(\Delta_n^2/4\).  The sum of the two testing-error probabilities is at least
\(1-\lVert Q_{n,+}-Q_{n,-}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\).  Since vector squared error dominates the squared projected error,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal N_n(P_0,\kappa(P_0))}
 E_P\lVert\widetilde\tau_n-\tau(P)\rVert^2
 \geq\frac{\Delta_n^2}{8}(1-2^{-1/2}).
\tag{6}
\]
Take the infimum over estimators, multiply by \(n/L_n\), use (4), and take the lower limit.  This yields the asserted positive constant \(c_0(P_0)\) and completes the matched upper and lower bounds.
